report.tagline: India's biggest UPI payments app, which now tries to make money from loans, insurance, investments and merchant tools on top of free payments.
report.simpleSummary: PhonePe is the app most Indians use to pay with UPI: scan a QR code at a chai stall, send money to a friend, or pay a bill. Sending money is free, so PhonePe earns almost nothing on most payments. It makes money by selling things on top: loans, insurance, mutual funds, speaker boxes for shops and ads. It is owned mostly by Walmart and has been preparing to list on the Indian stock market.

overview.whatItDoes: PhonePe lets people send and receive money through UPI, India's government-backed instant payments system, and pay bills and recharges. Merchants get free QR codes and paid Smart Speakers that announce each payment aloud. On top of payments, PhonePe distributes loans from partner lenders, sells insurance and mutual funds, runs a stock trading app (Share.Market) and an Android app store (Indus Appstore).
howItWorks: Link your bank account with your phone number and set a UPI PIN.
Scan any UPI QR code or enter a phone number to pay; money moves instantly between banks.
Shops get a free QR code and can rent a Smart Speaker for about ₹100 to ₹150 a month.
PhonePe uses payment history to offer loans from partner banks and NBFCs, earning a fee per loan.
Users can buy insurance, mutual funds, gold and stocks inside the app or linked apps.
Most UPI payments earn no fee because of India's zero-charge rule (zero MDR).
overview.valueProposition: Pay anyone in India, anywhere, instantly and free, from one trusted app that also handles bills, loans and savings.

businessModel.summary: PhonePe earns almost nothing on regular UPI payments because the government bans fees on them. It makes money from government incentives, merchant devices and payment services, and above all from selling financial products: loans, insurance and investments. In FY26 it still lost ₹2,792 crore. A 2026 rule adds a 0.4 percent fee on larger merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000, which could change this if it starts as planned.

revenueStreams.detail: Fees from partner lenders for loans given through PhonePe: ₹945 crore in FY26.
Smart Speaker rentals, payment gateway fees on cards and wallets, and fees from large merchants.
Commissions on insurance (₹191 crore) and broking and investments (₹108 crore) in FY26.
Payments from the government to support UPI growth, which change each year.

revenueStreams.stream: Bill payments, ads and Indus Appstore
revenueStreams.detail: Commissions on recharges and bills, ads in the app, and app store fees.

businessModel.pricing: UPI payments are free for users and small merchants. Smart Speaker rental is about ₹100 to ₹150 a month (varies). Loans, insurance and investments carry the provider's pricing; PhonePe earns a commission.
costDrivers: Employee costs, including large stock option expenses
Technology and servers to handle billions of payments a month
Merchant devices and field sales teams
businessModel.unitEconomics: PhonePe handles billions of UPI payments a month but earns close to ₹0 on most of them. With roughly ₹7,920 crore revenue and several hundred million monthly users, it earns about ₹150 to ₹200 per active user a year, while spending more than that. The money comes from a small share of users: a merchant renting a speaker pays about ₹1,500 a year, and a loan of ₹50,000 might earn PhonePe ₹1,000 to ₹2,000 in fees. The bet is to sell more of these to its huge base. Rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Word of mouth: people download it to pay or receive money from others
QR codes at almost every shop in India
Field sales teams signing up merchants in small towns
Cashback and offers in early years
whatBringsUsersBack: Paying many times a day for small things
growth.moat: PhonePe's moat is scale: about half of all UPI payments and over 47 million merchants. Its QR codes are everywhere, and merchants are used to its speakers. Payment data helps it decide who to lend to. But UPI is open, so users can switch apps easily.

improvementIdeas.idea: Instant auto-refund tracker with a clear timeline for failed payments

improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer support tickets and more trust.

improvementIdeas.idea: Limit cross-sell pop-ups to one per week and target them by real need
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher acceptance rate and less irritation.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Loan offer acceptance and uninstall rate

improvementIdeas.idea: Merchant credit line that grows with daily UPI sales, repaid automatically from settlements
improvementIdeas.problem: Small shops need flexible working capital.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More merchant loans with lower default.

improvementIdeas.idea: Scam warning when a user is about to pay a new contact a large amount after a call
improvementIdeas.problem: UPI fraud hurts users and trust.

pmLessons: A free product can win the market, but you need a plan to make money on top of it.
Cross-selling works only if users trust you; too many offers can push them away.
Regulation can change the game overnight. Know which rules your business depends on.
Scale is valuable, but profit per user matters when you go public.

interviewQuestions.question: UPI is free. How should PhonePe make money?
interviewQuestions.hint: List streams: lending, insurance, wealth, merchants, ads. Compare revenue per user and risk. Pick one to grow and how to measure it.

interviewQuestions.question: If NPCI enforces the 30 percent UPI cap, what should PhonePe do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Think about which users to keep (high value), how to shift focus to financial services, and how to protect merchants. Discuss trade-offs.

interviewQuestions.question: Paytm is profitable and PhonePe is not. Why, and what should PhonePe learn?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare merchant soundbox revenue, lending model and costs. Discuss growth versus profit strategy.

interviewQuestions.question: What is PhonePe's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Active users of a second financial service. Break into active payers, cross-sell rate, merchant monetisation and trust.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to reduce UPI fraud.
interviewQuestions.hint: Identify common scams (fake collect requests, call scams). Propose warnings, delays or limits for risky patterns. Track fraud rate and payment success.
